sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Checks before launching
sections.what: Confirms setup was done, activates the environment, installs streamlit if missing, and confirms app.py is present. If setup is missing, it prints the steps and waits for Enter.
sections.why: Likely reason: people who skipped setup get guidance instead of a confusing crash.
sections.watch_out: The streamlit fallback uses a plain install that is not matched to requirements.txt and hides any errors.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Starting the app
sections.what: Prints instructions about the Local URL and Ctrl+C, starts the page with streamlit, and prints a stopped message when it closes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the terminal stays open, so the user knows where to look and how to stop it.
sections.watch_out: The script never changes folder, so it must be started from the project folder or the app cannot find its data folders.

summary: A launcher script that checks setup and then starts the proposal web page.
purpose: Gives a one-step way to open the app on Mac or Linux.
why: The header says it is meant to be double-clicked. Likely reason: so non-programmers can start the app without typing commands.
how: Checks that the venv folder exists, activates it, installs streamlit if missing, checks that app.py exists, prints instructions, then starts streamlit with app.py and prints a stopped message when it ends.
inputs: The venv folder made by setup.sh and the app.py file.
outputs: A running web page at a local address shown in the terminal.
risks: It checks only the current folder, so starting it from another folder fails. The fallback install adds an unpinned version of streamlit.
debug: If it says setup is required, run setup.sh. If it says app.py was not found, move into the project folder. If the page does not open, copy the Local URL from the terminal. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop.
